description: §7.6 rule (b) / §66.7.6 rule 5 (S482) — the cell `c`'s seed reads `k` and `n`. `k`'s initializer runs in its place after the body-top write `n = 5` (6); the seed runs at the cell's declaration, where `n` is 5 (11) — not later, where the next statement sets `n` to 9 (15), and not before the body (`k` unset, `n` 1); then `z` — the log is `kz` and `@c` is 11. Before S482 construction ran the seed before the body. (s482-value-no-write r1, #2096 review INFO: the seed writes nothing — a seed is a value position, §6.15 A1 — and pins its place by what it reads; the spine initializers `k` and `z` still may write, A2. The writing seed is body-top-seed-computed-in-place-writes-neg.)
rationale: §7.6 rule (b) (S482): "A cell's initializer (its seed) runs at the cell's place in the run — where its declaration stands in the program body". ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S481-run-order-followups item 1 — "each seed is computed at its place in the sequence; records are still created at construction, so component identity (L12) is unchanged; a read of a seed before its place computes it early, on demand. Amends §66.7.6 rule 5." (owner: "yes, adopt your recs on all three"). s482-value-no-write: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S482-runorder-model-c A1/A2.
